root_cause.text: The nau8821 driver does not cancel or synchronize the delayed jack detection workqueue (`nau8821_jdet_work`) during component removal, causing a use-after-free when the work executes after the driver structures have been freed.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "Attempting to unload the driver while a jack detection work is pending would likely crash the kernel" and the crash trace shows the workqueue executing `nau8821_jdet_work` which calls `snd_soc_dapm_disable_pin` after the driver has been unloaded. The patch adds `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&nau8821->jdet_work)` in the new `nau8821_component_remove()` callback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a component remove callback to cancel pending jack detection work on driver removal to prevent use-after-free.
intent_record.what: Added a new function `nau8821_component_remove` that cancels the delayed work `nau8821->jdet_work` if `jdet_active` is true.
intent_record.how: This function ensures that any pending jack detection work is stopped before the component is removed, preventing potential use-after-free or work item execution after the driver data is freed.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the `nau8821_i2c_remove` function (line ~1698), the code only calls `devm_free_irq` but does not cancel or synchronize the workqueue `nau8821->jdet_work` (initialized via `INIT_WORK` in `nau8821_enable_jack_detect` at line ~1579). Consequently, if the work item is still pending or executing after driver removal, it will access freed driver structures (e.g., `nau8821->jack`, `nau8821->regmap`), causing a use-after-free. The missing `cancel_work_sync` makes this commit introduce the vulnerability.
